questions.question: Run B must start from master plus exactly one variant commit. This branch already carries the last session's decision-log commit, and this session will add its own log. Where do the logs go?

options.label: Logs to master first (Recommended)
options.description: Small separate PR with both decision logs, merged before run B. The variant branch is then rebased to one commit that touches only ship/SKILL.md, so run B's base is clean and its recorded commit pair is accurate.

options.label: Fold into variant commit
options.description: Squash everything into one commit on the variant branch. It's simpler, but the logs never reach master unless they're cherry-picked later, and the variant commit touches sdd/decisions/ too.

options.label: Leave as two commits
options.description: Keep c97968c3d below the variant commit. Run B would then start from master + 2 commits, a small departure from RFC-0020's stated start condition.

questions.question: P2 needs the build session to stop at PR open and a fresh session to take over. How should the second session start?

options.label: /clear, then /ship resume <PR> (Recommended)
options.description: Same terminal and worktree. /clear gives a new transcript and session ID. The handoff lives in the worktree's tmp/ship-handoff-<PR>.md (gitignored, copied into token-kit runs/ for the record). The second prompt is fixed in advance like the first.

options.label: New terminal, /ship resume <PR>
options.description: A fully separate claude process in the same worktree. Same effect on context as /clear, just more manual steps.

options.label: Handoff committed to the trace
options.description: The handoff goes into the BK-418/BUG-280 trace instead of tmp/, so it's durable on the PR. It adds trace content reviewers read, which is a small priming risk.

questions.question: P4: how long may a background wait run before the session reports and stops waiting? Run A's foreground gate had a median of 194 s, the tool limit is 600 s, and the stall was 37 min.

options.label: 15 min (Recommended)
options.description: About 4.6× the median gate and 1.5× the tool limit. It would have cut run A's 37-min stall to 15.

options.label: 10 min
options.description: Tighter. It risks cutting off a legitimately slow full suite under load.

options.label: 30 min
options.description: Loose. It barely changes run A's 37-min case.

questions.question: How much review should the variant get before run B? A wrong variant wastes a ~$50–140 run, and every review pass spends tokens.

options.label: Draft PR, your review only (Recommended)
options.description: Open it as a draft PR marked 'do not merge' so the diff has a review surface, and skip /rvw-pr. You read it and I fix what you flag. It's the cheapest option, and what matters is whether it says what RFC-0020 says, which you know best.

options.label: Draft PR + one /rvw-pr pass
options.description: One unprimed reviewer checks the diff against RFC-0020 § Proposal. Moderate cost, and it catches mechanism text that is inert or contradicts the Stop rule.

options.label: Branch only, no PR
options.description: Push the branch, no PR. That's minimal, but there's no record of the variant's review.

questions.question: How much review should the variant get before run B? A wrong variant wastes a ~$50–140 run, and every review pass spends tokens.
How should RFC-0020 Phase 0 proceed, given that run B on BUG-280 mostly measures P2 against unknown run-to-run noise and can't measure P3 cleanly?

options.label: Offline P2 + variant on real work (Recommended)
options.description: Drop run B. First derive P2's counterfactual from run A's transcript for free. Then run the variant on the next 2–3 real /ship items, including one prose-heavy one for P1, measured against the 41-PR corpus. Needs a small RFC-0020 amendment to Phase 0 and the decision rule. Merge #1093 now and close #1101's role as run B.

options.label: Offline P2 only, then decide
options.description: Do just the free counterfactual from run A's transcript now, and decide about any paid run once its number is in. No RFC change yet; #1093 stays a draft until then.

options.label: Run B as planned
options.description: Spend ~$50–140 after the 2026-10-15 reset. The comparison stays controlled on item, but P3 is contaminated by your knowledge of run A, P1 is barely exercised, and a gap under ~30% can't be told from noise.

questions.question: Rework RFC-0020 and the variant as proposed?

options.label: Yes, as proposed (Recommended)
options.description: P1 → claim discipline (scope rule, delete-not-narrow, check-closed prose every round); baseline = run A route 2 (27.8 M, 6 rounds, 49 findings); P3 used only to align scope. RFC PR to master first, then #1101 updated, then route-2 baseline and fix-commit classifier derived before run B.

options.label: Yes, but keep run A route 1 as baseline
options.description: Same P1 rewrite, but compare against the 31.5 M first route as the RFC says now. Scopes differ, so P1' and P2 effects mix with the narrowing.

options.label: Rules 1–2 only, no check-closing
options.description: Keep every review gate as master has it; only reduce what prose gets written and how it's fixed. Smaller ADR change (no clause amended), smaller expected saving.

questions.question: Where do the fixes land before run B?

options.label: Master, except (c) (Recommended)
options.description: Gate tooling, orientation, P2 handoff and claim rules (a)+(b) merge to master and help every session now. Only check-closed prose (c), which overrides ADR-0033/34/35/37 clauses, stays on the unmerged variant until run B confirms it; then an ADR amends them. Run B = master + the (c) commit.

options.label: Everything to master
options.description: Including (c), with an ADR amendment written up front on run A's evidence. Simplest run B (plain master), but amends the ADR chain before run B has shown (c) works.

options.label: Everything on the variant
options.description: Keep master unchanged as originally planned; all fixes ride the unmerged branch. Other sessions don't benefit until after run B and Phase 1.

questions.question: Is the order gate → orientation → claim discipline → run-B prerequisites right?

options.label: Yes, that order (Recommended)
options.description: Cheap reliability first so later sessions don't stall; then the biggest token lever; then the widest change.

options.label: Orientation first
options.description: Start with the biggest lever; gate tooling after. Steps 2–3 then run on today's unreliable gate.

options.label: Claim discipline first
options.description: Prose churn hits cloud sessions too, so fix it first for the widest effect; orientation and gate after.

How should sessions A, B and C be started?

options.label: I write 3 prompt files (Recommended)
options.description: One short prompt each in K:\Code\sandbox\token-kit\prompts\ (A-gate.md, B-orient.md, C-prereqs.md): goal, scope, branch name, gates to run, what not to touch, 'read UNDERSTANDING.md first'. You paste each into a fresh session. This session then stops working on the topic.

options.label: This session does one of them
options.description: I write prompts for two and take one myself (e.g. C, since I already read run A's PR). Saves one kickoff, but this session's context is already large, so every call costs more.

options.label: Only A and B for now
options.description: Prompts for gate and orientation only; C waits until they merge.
